entries.singular: Right so, a fine notice.  Rubik's mother-twice, she were a woman o'th'old kind.  And were her mate, and Rubik's father-twice.  Rubik's father-mother, she were a gran, a fitty bit of ol' London-Town, right so, but Rubik had a jaryi and a taita and a tamoi." Rubik's voice goes distant for a moment.  "An' they was all there, right to the end.  Standin' by, we were, one and all." They pause, then seem to snap back.  "No time for stories, kennit?  Back to the here an' now.
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line

. so was my father's father.  My father's mother, she was a grandma, a little
. piece of old London-Town, but I had a jaryi and a taita and a tamoi (these
. are words for grandparents in a guarani dialect).  They were all there,
. right to the end.  Standing by, we were, one and all.  No time for stories,
. though.  Back to the here and now.

entries.singular: &Before you stands a towering mass of metal, at least seven feet high, with a large reflective glass plate in the center of its torso.  It turns as you enter the room, and raises its hand in a surprisingly natural motion of greeting.  A gravelly voice resonates from unseen speakers in the steel frame.  Its tone is bizarrely normal, in complete contrast with everything else around you.  "Oy, you ain't dead.  Lookin' t'trade?"  The accent sounds vaguely British, but not familiar; like a terrible imitation of Cockney.

entries.singular: Us call us the Exodii, eh?  An' other things, but that'n's good.  This're our home, such as it.  This'n's monicked as Rubik, and tassed with a trade an'.  You lookin' to trade?  Us'n's alay for the scrap, metal an' more as it be.
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
. ~ We call ourselves the Exodii, eh?  And other things, but that's good.
. This is our home, such as it is.  I'm called Rubik, and I've been assigned
. to trade with you.  Are you looking to trade?  We're always looking for
. scrap, metal and more.
entries.catalogKey: ["","Us call us the Exodii, eh?  An' other things, but that'n's good.  This're our home, such as it.  This'n's monicked as Rubik, and tassed with a trade an'.  You lookin' to trade?  Us'n's alay for the scrap, metal an' more as it be."]

entries.singular: Good an' fine, then.
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
entries.catalogKey: ["","Good an' fine, then."]

entries.singular: Have it as ye'll see.
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
entries.catalogKey: ["","Have it as ye'll see."]

entries.singular: That be a right welcher, eh?  Afore us'n were to this land, the preface were on a half-score century by the reckonin'.  Landed us in amidst of a war'd turned wrong, for an' as the dead had come back in.  By the butcher's block, not much an unusual case, really.  The Enemy makes us fight.  By an' by, we came in, an' by then the killin' fields were plump and ready to harvest the bronze.  'Tain't no steel-of-the-lake, but 'tis a good dross metal for holdin' off a nibblin' mouth, so we kept a few o' their vestments an' stickers for to trade.
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
. ~ It's a bit of a surprise, isn't it?  Before we came here, we were in a
. place about 600 years earlier in time, or so.  We landed in the middle of a
. war that turned wrong when the dead started joining back in.  Truth be
. told, not a very unusual situation.  The Enemy makes us fight.  By and by,
. we came in, and by then the killing fields were ready for us to harvest
. their bronze.  It's not Avalonian steel, but it's a good strong metal for
. stopping a nibbling mouth, so we kept some of their armor and weapons to
. trade.
entries.catalogKey: ["","That be a right welcher, eh?  Afore us'n were to this land, the preface were on a half-score century by the reckonin'.  Landed us in amidst of a war'd turned wrong, for an' as the dead had come back in.  By the butcher's block, not much an unusual case, really.  The Enemy makes us fight.  By an' by, we came in, an' by then the killin' fields were plump and ready to harvest the bronze.  'Tain't no steel-of-the-lake, but 'tis a good dross metal for holdin' off a nibblin' mouth, so we kept a few o' their vestments an' stickers for to trade."]

entries.singular: Ah, a real monger's eye, ye be.  Them's the mettle o' many a year of trials.  Us'n've been clashin wi' the Enemy for a long an' then, an' o'er the turns us've worked out some vestments for the job.  Keep's a walker walkin' longer, an I'm ken.  This'n keeps some o' the parst in an' around, but ye'd be tassed to make the vestment with the grease o' your own brow.
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
. ~ Ah, you've got a discerning eye.  They're the result of many years of
. work.  We've been fighting the Enemy for a long time, and over the years
. we've worked out some armor for the job.  Keeps you going a bit longer in
. the field, if you ask me.  I keep some of the parts in stock, but you'll
. have to put it together yourself.
entries.catalogKey: ["","Ah, a real monger's eye, ye be.  Them's the mettle o' many a year of trials.  Us'n've been clashin wi' the Enemy for a long an' then, an' o'er the turns us've worked out some vestments for the job.  Keep's a walker walkin' longer, an I'm ken.  This'n keeps some o' the parst in an' around, but ye'd be tassed to make the vestment with the grease o' your own brow."]

entries.singular: This 'n that, an I'm ken.  It be made for a fine wander, beladen with the goods o' the hunt, y'see.  By which I'm to say, 'tis well suited to carry all ye can wrest from the cold arms o' the deadlands, without troublin' your gait nor makin' it easy for the cold clutch o' the scrabblin' arm.  Be an' it is tough as a tarket's nut, I'd razz.
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
. ~ This and that, you know.  It's made for a traveling scavenger, you see.
. What I mean is, it's well suited to carry around whatever you pick up in
. the wastelands, without making it too hard to get around nor giving any
. easy handholds for scrambling arms.  That, and I'd say it's as tough as
. nails.
entries.catalogKey: ["","This 'n that, an I'm ken.  It be made for a fine wander, beladen with the goods o' the hunt, y'see.  By which I'm to say, 'tis well suited to carry all ye can wrest from the cold arms o' the deadlands, without troublin' your gait nor makin' it easy for the cold clutch o' the scrabblin' arm.  Be an' it is tough as a tarket's nut, I'd razz."]

entries.singular: 'Tis as simple as comes to a wobble.  Our vestment be oft made from the fine clothes and hides of the land, and our jibber tears the stuff o' life apart here and there when us'n travel.  For as some can be saved if care be taken, there be no case to store nigh enough o' this.  That, an' our manuc-makers run as hot as a sunstone, no spit'n taste for that which we don't use usselves.
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
. ~ It's a simple matter of how we teleport.  Our clothes are often made from
. cloth and hides from wherever we visit, and our teleporter tears living
. stuff apart here and there when we travel.  Some can be saved if we take
. care, but there's no room to store nearly enough extra.  That, and our
. fabricators are always busy, no time to waste on stuff we don't need for
. ourselves.
entries.catalogKey: ["","'Tis as simple as comes to a wobble.  Our vestment be oft made from the fine clothes and hides of the land, and our jibber tears the stuff o' life apart here and there when us'n travel.  For as some can be saved if care be taken, there be no case to store nigh enough o' this.  That, an' our manuc-makers run as hot as a sunstone, no spit'n taste for that which we don't use usselves."]

entries.singular: HEH, ye c'nnae get enough o' ol' Rubik's merchandise, eh?  Sure as 'ell, come back in <interval>.
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
. ~ HEH, you can't get enough of old Rubik's merchandise, eh?  Sure as hell,
. come back in <interval>.
entries.catalogKey: ["","HEH, ye c'nnae get enough o' ol' Rubik's merchandise, eh?  Sure as 'ell, come back in <interval>."]

entries.singular: Sure as you c'n try.  Us're not the greatest yarker, nor do it all for gratis, kennit.
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
. ~ You can surely try.  I'm not the greatest speaker, and I won't just chat
. forever for free, you know.
entries.catalogKey: ["","Sure as you c'n try.  Us're not the greatest yarker, nor do it all for gratis, kennit."]

entries.singular: Sure as can," the gravelly voice takes on an unmistakeable 'customer service' tone.  "What'll ye tass this'n for?
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
. ~ Of course, what can I do for you?
entries.catalogKey: ["","Sure as can,\" the gravelly voice takes on an unmistakeable 'customer service' tone.  \"What'll ye tass this'n for?"]

entries.singular: Aye, business afore, 'tis said.  What'll ye tass to ol' Rubik?
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
. ~ Business before pleasure.  What do you need?
entries.catalogKey: ["","Aye, business afore, 'tis said.  What'll ye tass to ol' Rubik?"]

entries.singular: Nah, mate, still operatin'.
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
entries.catalogKey: ["","Nah, mate, still operatin'."]

entries.singular: Gimme spek, 'n  fetch 'em 'ere.
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
. ~ Give me a second, and I'll bring them here.
entries.catalogKey: ["","Gimme spek, 'n  fetch 'em 'ere."]

entries.singular: Lemme poke.  Will tass what ye can for a shiny.
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
. ~ Let me see.  Will do what I can for a coin.
entries.catalogKey: ["","Lemme poke.  Will tass what ye can for a shiny."]

entries.singular: Fer this 'un, I can yank out their bits 'n give 'em to ya, or I can jus' take out the busted pieces so they can still use th' rest o' stuff in 'em. Elsewise, why don't ya jest give 'im to me?  I reckon I can turn 'im into a right useful worker.
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
. ~ For this one, I can pull out their CBM and give any working to you, or I
. can just take out broken bits so that they will still be able to use the
. rest of stuff in them.  Alternatively, why don't you just give them to me?
. I surely can help them adjust to life as a cyborg.
entries.catalogKey: ["","Fer this 'un, I can yank out their bits 'n give 'em to ya, or I can jus' take out the busted pieces so they can still use th' rest o' stuff in 'em. Elsewise, why don't ya jest give 'im to me?  I reckon I can turn 'im into a right useful worker."]

entries.singular: This 'unwon't be twitching', too much grey lost to dead.  But ye can salvage bits from 'em or born 'em for a walker, or just cut out the rot 'n grey link so ya can miss 'em proper.
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
. ~ This one can't be saved, too much brain rotted.  But I can salvage bits
. from them or repurpose them for walker, or just cut out rot and neural
. interface so you can bury them proper.
entries.catalogKey: ["","This 'unwon't be twitching', too much grey lost to dead.  But ye can salvage bits from 'em or born 'em for a walker, or just cut out the rot 'n grey link so ya can miss 'em proper."]

entries.singular: Thank ye.  When you an' Rubik first met, how long'd it been since the mess begun?
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
entries.catalogKey: ["","Thank ye.  When you an' Rubik first met, how long'd it been since the mess begun?"]

entries.singular: Lovely!  Benzete's gonna be a pair, that's a track!  I mean, they'll be right happy.  This is their first jump, and it's a flappin' duck.
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
. ~ Lovely!  Benzete (this is a name) is going to be beside themselves,
. that's for sure.  I mean, they'll be really happy.  This is their first
. jump, and it's a lucky one.
entries.catalogKey: ["","Lovely!  Benzete's gonna be a pair, that's a track!  I mean, they'll be right happy.  This is their first jump, and it's a flappin' duck."]

entries.singular: So 'twere an I recalt, us're yarkin' of Benzete an' their great first jump.
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
. ~ As I recall, we were talking about Benzete and how this is a great jump
. for their first time.
entries.catalogKey: ["","So 'twere an I recalt, us're yarkin' of Benzete an' their great first jump."]

entries.singular: Us gotta leave the old world afore it's worn right to the gums, an y'ken, and find a nice twitchy one on t'other side.  Your deadland be a brand shiny
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
. ~ We've got to leave the old world before it gets too worn out, you see,
. and find a nice fresh one on the other side.  Your deadland is as fresh as
. it gets.
entries.catalogKey: ["","Us gotta leave the old world afore it's worn right to the gums, an y'ken, and find a nice twitchy one on t'other side.  Your deadland be a brand shiny"]

entries.singular: Neverken.  Right and so, the Enemy is new here, and us'n have a few good hours in the sun beforenext the jump.
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
. ~ No worries.  I mean, the Enemy is new here, and we have a bit of safe
. time ahead of us before we have to jump away again.
entries.catalogKey: ["","Neverken.  Right and so, the Enemy is new here, and us'n have a few good hours in the sun beforenext the jump."]

entries.singular: That be a part an' switch, but this be'n nice for all, overtop the last jump by heads.  Otherlands with fusillies and mobbings, us'n gets a fine change on that.
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
. ~ That's a part of it, sure, but this is nice for other reasons, and much
. better than our last jump.  Otherlands with fusillies and mobbings are
. really useful to us.
entries.catalogKey: ["","That be a part an' switch, but this be'n nice for all, overtop the last jump by heads.  Otherlands with fusillies and mobbings, us'n gets a fine change on that."]

entries.singular: You kennit rightly!  That and this be'n nice for all, overtop the last jump by heads.  Otherlands with fusillies and mobbings, us'n gets a fine change on that.
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
. ~ That's exactly it!  This is nice for many reasons, and much better than
. our last jump.  Otherlands with fusillies and mobbings are really useful to
. us.
entries.catalogKey: ["","You kennit rightly!  That and this be'n nice for all, overtop the last jump by heads.  Otherlands with fusillies and mobbings, us'n gets a fine change on that."]

entries.singular: Oh, rights.  Many lands be'd assert on thosun's.  A fusilly, she's a weapon, shoots a shot at high speeds usin' bang.  A mobbing, he's a grand box o' metal, pushed by burnin' and boomin' from wit'in, kennit?
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
. ~ Oh, yeah.  Lots of places have different words for those.  A fusilly is a
. weapon that fires a bullet at high speeds using propellant.  A mobbing is a
. big metal box that's moved around by an internal explosion.  Do you get it?
entries.catalogKey: ["","Oh, rights.  Many lands be'd assert on thosun's.  A fusilly, she's a weapon, shoots a shot at high speeds usin' bang.  A mobbing, he's a grand box o' metal, pushed by burnin' and boomin' from wit'in, kennit?"]

entries.singular: Right so, us'n'll write it in the dicky.  Here, a shiny brass farthing for crossin' the nation.
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
. ~ Great, I'll put that in the dictionary.  Here's a token of my gratitude
. for your explanation.
entries.catalogKey: ["","Right so, us'n'll write it in the dicky.  Here, a shiny brass farthing for crossin' the nation."]

entries.singular: Them's an otherlander from thrice jumps an' change, wide as the sky.  They's got happily on sommat for the tracking, you ken?
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
. ~ They're an otherlander from around three jumps ago, a real optimistic
. greenhorn.  They're really interested in how we do tracking, you see?
entries.catalogKey: ["","Them's an otherlander from thrice jumps an' change, wide as the sky.  They's got happily on sommat for the tracking, you ken?"]

entries.singular: Hmm.  They… planned out the last jump?  Like as an apprentice to the ol' sexten.
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
. ~ Like an apprentice to the old tracker.
entries.catalogKey: ["","Hmm.  They… planned out the last jump?  Like as an apprentice to the ol' sexten."]

entries.singular: Sure an' that's a fine enough word, an I'm ken.
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
. ~ Sure, that word is fine, I think.
entries.catalogKey: ["","Sure an' that's a fine enough word, an I'm ken."]

entries.singular: Yeah, you could call us as it.  Us're from otherlands mostlike.  Not otherworlds though.  Too risky bringin' them squelchies into the fold.
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
. ~ Yeah, you could say that.  We're from otherlands, most of the time.  Not
. otherworlds though.  Too risky bringing those monsters into our safe haven.
entries.catalogKey: ["","Yeah, you could call us as it.  Us're from otherlands mostlike.  Not otherworlds though.  Too risky bringin' them squelchies into the fold."]

entries.singular: Sure an that's a biggun'.  Otherworlds be the wherefore o' them uggo buggers you got round and here, eh?  Walkin' plants and talkin' mushrooms and whatlike.  Otherlands be tassed more of a kinship.  I be from Earth, but my Earth be differed.  So you's shouldno be asked what the Exodii is doin' on Earth, because some is feelin' of us fine an' fine at home, an I'm ken.  You's should be askin' what the Exodii is doin' razzin up your green and brown.
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
. ~ Yeah, that's a big question.  Otherworlds are how you got those ugly bug-
. creatures around here, you know?  Walking plants, talking mushroom, stuff
. like that.  Otherlands are closer related.  I'm from Earth, just a
. different Earth.  You shouldn't be asking what the Exodii are doing in
. Earth, because some of us are feeling pretty at home here, I think.  You
. should be asking what we're doing hanging out in your part of town.
entries.catalogKey: ["","Sure an that's a biggun'.  Otherworlds be the wherefore o' them uggo buggers you got round and here, eh?  Walkin' plants and talkin' mushrooms and whatlike.  Otherlands be tassed more of a kinship.  I be from Earth, but my Earth be differed.  So you's shouldno be asked what the Exodii is doin' on Earth, because some is feelin' of us fine an' fine at home, an I'm ken.  You's should be askin' what the Exodii is doin' razzin up your green and brown."]

entries.singular: *becomes distant for a moment.  "Ah.  Home.  It were a long time gone, kennit.  Your'n be not too far.  This'n… I don't think I want to talk 'bout it.  Too much metal atwixt now an' then."
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
. ~ Ah.  Home.  That's a long time gone, you know?  Yours isn't too
. different.  I… don't think I want to talk about it.  I've changed too much
. between then and now."
entries.catalogKey: ["","*becomes distant for a moment.  \"Ah.  Home.  It were a long time gone, kennit.  Your'n be not too far.  This'n… I don't think I want to talk 'bout it.  Too much metal atwixt now an' then.\""]

entries.singular: Us'n saw this were a pidgeon's road, I'd razz.  Only one way, I'm ken, if I'm not to join the rank an' file.
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
. ~ I realized that it was a no-brainer question.  There was only one other
. option, you see, if I didn't join the Exodii.
entries.catalogKey: ["","Us'n saw this were a pidgeon's road, I'd razz.  Only one way, I'm ken, if I'm not to join the rank an' file."]

entries.singular: Robot?  What assert is f'r it?  Ahold…"  Rubik stops for a moment, as if thinking.  "Ah, an automate?  No, this'n be flesh 'n blood as ye be, encased in a shell o' metal an' wire.  Not so much flesh as there were.  The wire is amixed an' afloat with the flesh, all as one, kennit."
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
. ~ Robot?  What does that word mean?  Hang on.  …Ah, an automate?  No, I'm
. as flesh and blood as you are, encased in a shell of metal and wire.  Not
. as much flesh as there used to be.  The wire is mixed and woven into the
. flesh, all as one, you see.
entries.catalogKey: ["","Robot?  What assert is f'r it?  Ahold…\"  Rubik stops for a moment, as if thinking.  \"Ah, an automate?  No, this'n be flesh 'n blood as ye be, encased in a shell o' metal an' wire.  Not so much flesh as there were.  The wire is amixed an' afloat with the flesh, all as one, kennit.\""]

entries.singular: Yeah, that be the soggy leaves, an I'm ken.  A bit o' both, but Rubik were once as a kin, to you be.
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
. ~ Yeah, that's the basic explanation.  A bit of both now, but I used to be
. just like you.
entries.catalogKey: ["","Yeah, that be the soggy leaves, an I'm ken.  A bit o' both, but Rubik were once as a kin, to you be."]

entries.singular: A junker base, innit?  Pile o' gamp.  Us'll pack it up and sing along soon enough.
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
. ~ A junker base, obviously.  A jury-rigged mess.  We'll pack it up and
. leave eventually.
entries.catalogKey: ["","A junker base, innit?  Pile o' gamp.  Us'll pack it up and sing along soon enough."]

entries.singular: Yon aforetime otherland, 'twere a right soggy biscuit.  This'n be crisp an' fresh yet.  Us'n'll try as might stay a fair tick.
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
. ~ The otherlands we were in before had only little time left, so we can't
. say for sure.  But this land is as fresh as it can be.
entries.catalogKey: ["","Yon aforetime otherland, 'twere a right soggy biscuit.  This'n be crisp an' fresh yet.  Us'n'll try as might stay a fair tick."]

entries.singular: For an' how, ye be needin' to think wi' them elevens o' directions, kennit?  Us'll open a gate an' wibble-an-wobble.  Same as us came.
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
. ~ To understand how, you've gotta think eleven-dimensionally.  We'll open
. up a gate and teleport out, the same as we came.
entries.catalogKey: ["","For an' how, ye be needin' to think wi' them elevens o' directions, kennit?  Us'll open a gate an' wibble-an-wobble.  Same as us came."]

entries.singular: 'Tis a good an' yark, sooth.  Them as can have the metal deep in, can be saved for the risen, but it b'ain't a sure course.  Some as comes back anyway, an' some be too much flesh.  The grander lot are no Exodii like ol' Rubik, most be friends more kin to thyself.  Us'll hearken out and trundle home the pieces for a scrub-and-bucket.
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
. ~ Ah, good question.  Enough cybernetic implants can keep someone from
. coming back as a zombie, but it's not a sure thing.  Some come back anyway,
. and some just don't have enough cybernetics.  Most of them aren't full
. Exodii like old Rubik, they're more our friends - like you.  Sooner or
. later we'll get out there, put them down, and bring their parts back for
. cleaning.
entries.catalogKey: ["","'Tis a good an' yark, sooth.  Them as can have the metal deep in, can be saved for the risen, but it b'ain't a sure course.  Some as comes back anyway, an' some be too much flesh.  The grander lot are no Exodii like ol' Rubik, most be friends more kin to thyself.  Us'll hearken out and trundle home the pieces for a scrub-and-bucket."]

entries.singular: Rubik's not the finest dandy to yark it, an I'm ken, but this'n'll do best as can.  Ol' Rubik an' the stompy-clanker gang be shiny an' fine as can be, for y'see so well, but on the wind-up, the guts be nigh so fleshy as they were afore, twixt as they be with wire and steel.  Ain't none so left as remembers precise how it all goes, and much is boggled from bits and drabs o' a dozen elsewheres.  'Tis a marked fine they work at all, though work they do, and nicely.  Still, 'tis hard to know what'll crumple out from the can.  Those as return, they be… less well made as ol' Rubik.  Some as did work themselves, even, and mayhap against the good old ways.
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
. ~ I don't think I'm the best to explain that, but I'll do my best.  Our
. technology might seem pretty high-tech and well made to you, but on the
. inside I'm still mostly human meat bound up in wires and steel.  Nobody's
. left that remembers exactly how it all goes, and much of it is cobbled
. together from a few different dimensions.  It's a miracle they work as well
. as they do, but somehow it's actually pretty functional.  Still, it can be
. hard to know exactly what could go wrong.  The ones who come back as
. zombies, they're generally less well made than me.  Some even did their own
. cybernetic conversions, and didn't exactly follow best practices.

Ol' Rubik an' the stompy-clanker gang be shiny an' fine as can be, for y'see so well, but on the wind-up, the guts be nigh so fleshy as they were afore, twixt as they be with wire and steel.  Ain't none so left as remembers precise how it all goes, and much is boggled from bits and drabs o' a dozen elsewheres.  'Tis a marked fine they work at all, though work they do, and nicely.  Still, 'tis hard to know what'll crumple out from the can.  Those as return, they be… less well made as ol' Rubik.  Some as did work themselves, even, and mayhap against the good old ways."]

entries.singular: *'s tone changes slightly, sounding a bit pained.  "Ah, them be an in-between, more machiner.  Us'n use the softer bits o' other critters for them, an' there be a manufactory for the walker.  A hard but needed choice."
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
entries.catalogKey: ["","*'s tone changes slightly, sounding a bit pained.  \"Ah, them be an in-between, more machiner.  Us'n use the softer bits o' other critters for them, an' there be a manufactory for the walker.  A hard but needed choice.\""]

entries.singular: Blinker than a bat, but downer than a cat.  Razzin' up the bits be a trick and some.  The draw-make automates can manufactorize the outer shell, and there be automates for the most o' the tools.  Some bits be more a breakfast o' rats, an' for them, us'n has some artisanals.  Us'n b'ain't on the solid now, so 'tis a longer down.
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
. ~ Faster than you might guess, but it can still take a while, the hardest
. part is sourcing the materials for one.  We've got printers that make the
. body, and others that make the tools and equipment the walker will use.
. Some of the special parts have to be manufactured by hand, so we have a
. small team that does that.  Right now, it's very slow, we're still setting
. up our operations.
entries.catalogKey: ["","Blinker than a bat, but downer than a cat.  Razzin' up the bits be a trick and some.  The draw-make automates can manufactorize the outer shell, and there be automates for the most o' the tools.  Some bits be more a breakfast o' rats, an' for them, us'n has some artisanals.  Us'n b'ain't on the solid now, so 'tis a longer down."]

entries.singular: *sounds thoughtful.  "This'n can't make a call o' the quarter.  The stompers be a king's necklace, and the manufactory don't run on dreams.  Mayhap when us'n be more on the solid, but for the tick and tumble, no."
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
. ~ I don't know about that.  Each one we make is very important to our

entries.singular:
F'r to wax religious, eh?

*Rubik pauses for a while.  When they start talking again, their voice is slow and more serious than usual.*

This'n can't tell ye, rightly, but those what have a bottle an' a cork what fits it, they yark about the Enemy.  Most folks got a story like that in their ol' hearth-tales, an I'm ken.  A bad way, from times old, come back.  Ol' Rubik don't know much about that, but something makes them bodies walk and moan, and it don't seem to be somethin' of the way o' our kin.  How it gets in, well, that be anyone's for a guess.  It can come the way we came, wibbling and wobbling, but it don't always.  How it be'd the end for your deadland, Rubik can't say for ye.
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line
. ~ You want to get religious, eh?  I can't tell you for sure, but the people
. who claim to know, they talk about the Enemy.  Most folks have a fairy tale
. like that, I think.  A monster from ancient memory, returned.  I don't know
. much about that, but something makes those bodies walk and moan, and it
. doesn't seem to be anything human.  How it gets in, well, that's anyone's
. guess.  It can come the way we came, through a portal, but it doesn't
. always.  How it was for your world, I can't tell you.

entries.singular: This be a deadland, kennit.  Spend a farthing at the pastor's house, d'ye razz?  What be left for ye?  The dead'll be in the fields, the forests, all around the green and brown.  Anything what walks, they'll salt 'n fallow, and most'll rise up and rejoin.  Those what don't, the Enemy twists and turns as well.  Every deadland be the same.  Ye've turns and twain, but come as it may, this land be dead.  Though, an I'm ken, ye've quite a few turns and twain to go yet.

. all over the world.  Anything that walks, they'll make it so it doesn't,
. and most will come back as undead.  Those that don't, the Enemy will change
. them as well.  Every deadland is the same.  You've years and more to go,
. but one way or another, this place is dead.  Though, as far as I can see,
. you've got quite a few years to go yet.

entries.singular:
*makes a stiff, bowing gesture and leads you out of the shop and down a stone pathway towards one of the larger buildings in the compound.  A thick steel door slides aside to reveal a gloomy, rust-dusted corridor.  At the end of the corridor is a clean appearing surgical suite, not too different from any other surgical suite aside from the dim lighting and the surgeon itself.  At the head of the surgical table is a contraption reminiscent of an upside-down spider, its multiple glistening medical limbs curling gently in eager anticipation of your approach.  You have little time to question your choices before you feel a sharp pinch in your left shoulder, and the world drifts away.

You awaken on a comfortable bed, your chest and throat sore but otherwise well.  As the haze of anesthesia fades, you notice several tiny, sore wounds on your chest and arms.  A humanoid cyborg, not Rubik, notices that you are awake and wordlessly gestures you to follow, leading you back to Rubik's store.

"Ah, an' you're with the stars 'n lights again, an I'm ken.  'Tis grand.  Those wee CBMs will do ye little an fine, but they are a start.  Now us'n can sell you all you like, an' help with install, should ye wish."
comments: . ~ NPC dialogue line

. and that for because they've traded their flesh for metal the fae aren't
. really interested in them anyway.  Not quite as bad as the undead but more
. tricksome.
